newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Higher Ed. (Denison Univ.) rated AA - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Higher Ed. (Denison Univ.) rated AA - S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp today said it has assigned its double-A' rating to Ohio Higher Educational Facility Commission's higher educational facilities revenue bonds series 1996, issued for Denison University.
The double-A' rating is based on:
-- Impressive liquidity, strong coverage, and financial flexibility provided by a large endowment valued at $213 million at fiscal year-end 1996 of which $126 million is unrestricted;
-- Tight budgetary control as evidenced by 43 years of operating surpluses;
-- Low debt burden with $2 million in loans outstanding and no additional debt plans; and
-- Strong governance and conservative management practices.

A higher rating is precluded by demand statistics, which are inconsistent with double-A' category ratings. The bonds are a general obligation of the college and are issued to provide financing for various improvements and renovations on campus. The university plans to pay for project costs from capital campaign proceeds.

Denison's $213 million endowment provides strong flexibility with $126 million unrestricted and available to support operations and debt. The endowment has grown from $17 million in 1976 to the current value through sound management, a conservative spending policy and strong support and guidance from the board. Unrestricted endowment provides coverage of 2.4 times (x) the operating budget and 4.4x pro forma debt. The endowment is managed by numerous outside managers, with 53% in equities, 19% in fixed income, 18% in hedge funds, and in 10% in alternative investments, and oversight remains with management and the board. Returns have been strong with five-year annualized returns of the total fund of 18.99% outperforming the S&P 500. Returns over the past five years have ranged from 5.9% in 1994 to 22.9% in 1995. The spending policy is 5% of the three-year moving average of market value of endowment; actual spending is lower at about 4.5%. Financial operations are stable and profitable, with balanced budgets for the past 43 years. Tuition discounting is high nearing 40%, however is not a concern given the university's financial flexibility.

Denison University, established in 1831, is a private liberal arts college located in Granville, Ohio. The college is small with a total enrollment at 2,031 in 1996. Denison's size, mission and goals have not changed significantly over time and the institution continues to strive toward providing a solid liberal arts education to high quality students. Admission statistics are adequate with a growing applicant pool, 82% accepted and strong student quality with average SAT scores of 1166 in 1995; however Denison continues to experience heavy competition as indicated by a weak matriculation rate at 31%.
The outlook reflects continued stable financial operations and prudent management and investment of the endowment, Standard & Poor's said.
